mcat_description.short: Agricultural greenhouses are prefabricated protected cultivation structures — primarily polyhouses with GI pipe frames and UV-stabilised polyethylene film covers — sold as complete erected structures or supply-and-erect projects for growing vegetables, flowers, and high-value crops under controlled climatic conditions.
mcat_description.long: Agricultural greenhouses in India are predominantly polyhouses: framed structures of galvanised iron (GI) pipes covered with UV-stabilised low-density polyethylene (LDPE) film of minimum 200 microns thickness, designed to create a controlled micro-climate for horticulture. The dominant commercial types are Naturally Ventilated Polyhouses (NVPH) and Climate Control Polyhouses (CCPH/Fan-Pad), with shade net houses and low-cost bamboo-frame structures serving the budget segment. Structures are designed and constructed as per BIS Standard IS 14462:1997 and polyfilm specifications per IS 15827:2009, and are eligible for government subsidies under the National Horticulture Mission (NHM) and National Horticulture Board (NHB). Buyers range from individual farmers and agri-entrepreneurs to institutional horticulture departments, and the product is sold on a per-square-metre basis for supply-and-erect turnkey projects.

market_context: Agricultural greenhouses in India are dominated by the polyhouse format — GI pipe frame structures covered with UV-stabilised LDPE film — which is the most popular greenhouse technology due to its low construction cost relative to glass or polycarbonate alternatives. The Bureau of Indian Standards has codified greenhouse design under IS 14462:1997 (layout, design and construction) and IS 15827:2009 (polyhouse film specifications). The National Horticulture Mission (NHM) and National Horticulture Board (NHB) provide capital subsidies of up to 50% for eligible polyhouse structures, with standardised model sizes ranging from 500 sq mt to 4,000 sq mt; this subsidy linkage is a major demand driver in the Indian market. Two primary commercial categories exist: Open Ventilated Polyhouse (OVPH/NVPH) for general horticulture, and Climate Control Polyhouse (CCPH/Fan-Pad) for premium off-season production. Shade net houses (HDPE net, 35–75% shading) are a distinct and widely adopted sub-type for summer vegetable and nursery applications. Key crops grown include tomato, capsicum, cucumber, rose, gerbera, and carnation. The market spans individual progressive farmers, agri-entrepreneurs, FPOs, and state horticulture departments. Structures must withstand wind loads of 110 km/h and 50 kg/sq mt wind pressure as per AP Horticulture guidelines, and live loads of 15 kg/sq mt.
